title: Visual Instruction Tuning & LLaVA
interviewAnswer: Visual instruction tuning adapts a vision-language model to follow natural-language instructions grounded in images. LLaVA is a classic example: it connects a CLIP vision encoder to an LLM through a projector and trains on image-instruction-response data so the model learns conversational visual reasoning.
why: Pretrained image-text alignment alone does not guarantee useful conversational instruction following.
intuition: CLIP teaches “which text matches this image?” Visual instruction tuning teaches “given this image and this question, how should I respond?”
deepDive: Training often begins by aligning a connector/projector while keeping large backbones frozen, then performs multimodal instruction tuning on richer conversations. Dataset construction, resolution, connector capacity and whether the vision/LLM backbones are frozen or fine-tuned all influence cost and quality.
workedExample: Input: an image of a chart plus “What trend appears after 2024?” Output: a grounded textual answer. The training pair teaches both image use and instruction style.
commonMistakes: Confusing contrastive image-text pretraining with generative visual instruction tuning.
Assuming instruction tuning removes visual hallucination.
followUps: What parameters would you freeze first?
How would you build multimodal instruction data?
production: Evaluate grounding, OCR/chart performance, refusal behavior and hallucination separately; text-only quality can hide weak visual dependence.
